title: Pharmacological Characterization of Vasomotor Responses in the Tree Shrew (Tupaia belangeri) Basilar Artery: A Promising Model for Human Cerebrovascular Research
content: The tree shrew (Tupaia belangeri) has emerged as a valuable experimental model for human disease research due to its close phylogenetic relationship with humans. Since the responsiveness of the basilar artery to endogenous vasoactive substances exhibits species-specific characteristics, we investigated the effects of vasoactive substances on isolated tupaia basilar arteries to determine whether this species is suitable as a human model. 5-Hydroxytryptamine (5-HT) and histamine (His) induced contraction, while bradykinin (BK) and acetylcholine (ACh) produced concentration-dependent relaxation. Pharmacological analysis revealed that 5-HT-induced contractions were mediated by 5-H1 and 5-HT2 receptors, and His-induced responses by H1 receptors. BK-induced relaxation was inhibited by the B2 antagonist HOE140 and Nω-nitro-L-arginine (L-NA), but not by B1 antagonists or indomethacin, suggesting a B2 receptor-mediated nitric oxide (NO) pathway. ACh-induced relaxation was significantly inhibited by L-NA and the M3 antagonist pFHHSiD, indicating M3 receptor-mediated NO release. At resting tone, L-NA induced contraction and indomethacin induced relaxation, suggesting basal regulation by NO and prostanoids. These findings demonstrate that 5-HT1/5-HT2 and H1 receptors mediate contraction, while B2 and M3 receptors mediate relaxation in the tupaia basilar artery. This study highlights species-specific cerebrovascular regulation and supports the tupaia as a relevant model for investigating human cerebrovascular physiology and pathophysiology.
